Standing pull requests now get auto-merge turned on when GitHub shows it unset, and are left alone when it's already on. The change is committed on `main` as `14a45b4`.

- **Code** (`src/branches/dispatch_fire.go`): `pullOpens` reads `auto_merge` and `node_id` off each listed pull. A standing pull with `auto_merge` null calls the enable mutation. The enable call moved into `takeAutoMerge`, which the opened-PR path also uses. A refusal from GitHub still gives the same red result and message as before.
- **Tests** (`dispatch_fire_test.go`): two new tests. One checks that an unset standing PR gets enabled by node id with no second PR posted. The other checks that a standing PR already holding auto-merge sees no GraphQL call.
- **Existing fixtures**: two existing "standing" tests (`dispatch_fire_test.go`, `dispatch_done_test.go`) had PRs with no `auto_merge` key, so they now read as unset and would send the enable call. I added `auto_merge` to their fixtures so they still test only the no-second-PR rule.

`go test ./...` passes. `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean on the branches package.

`./RUNME.sh check` exits 1, and it does the same on the base commit (`0145994`), which I ran in a temporary worktree. Its log has `Vale reads no file ... exit status -1`, and Vale isn't installed in this sandbox. I haven't confirmed that's the only cause of the exit code.

I left the ticket file `spec/tickets/standing-pull-takes-auto-merge.md` untouched.
